record.paper_title: Periods of Integrals on Algebraic Manifolds: Summary of Main Results and Discussion of Open Problems
record.original_question: How is the automorphic cohomology H^{q0}(D/T,O(K^mu)) of a period matrix domain quotient related to horizontal holomorphic maps S->D/T that arise from variations of Hodge structure, and can such automorphic cohomology be used to construct the automorphic forms needed to algebrize period images?

evidence.quote: what we quite naturally are led to is automorphic cohomology
Relate the automorphic cohomology H q o(D/Tf 0(K")) to the horizontal, holomorphic maps
can automorphic cohomology be used to construct the automorphic forms requested in (10.7)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $D = G_{\mathbb{R}}/T$ be a period matrix domain, i.e. the classifying space for polarized Hodge structures on a fixed real vector space with given Hodge numbers, where $G_{\mathbb{R}}$ is the real isometry group of the polarization and $T$ is the compact isotropy subgroup fixing a reference Hodge filtration. Let $\Gamma \subset G_{\mathbb{R}}$ be an arithmetic subgroup acting properly discontinuously on $D$, and write $X = \Gamma\backslash D$. For a dominant character $\mu$ of $T$, let $K^\mu \to D$ denote the associated $G_{\mathbb{R}}$-homogeneous holomorphic line bundle (a tensor power of the canonical bundle determined by $\mu$), descending to a line bundle on $X$ also denoted $\mathcal{O}(K^\mu)$. Let $q_0$ be the dimension of a maximal compact subvariety of $D$ (so that, in the non-classical case where $D$ is not Hermitian symmetric, the relevant cohomology occurs in middle degree $q_0 > 0$).

A horizontal holomorphic map $\Phi : S \to X$, from a quasi-projective complex manifold $S$, is one whose differential takes values in the horizontal tangent subbundle of $D$ (equivalently, $\Phi$ arises as the period map of a polarized variation of Hodge structure over $S$).

(a) Describe the relationship between the automorphic cohomology group $H^{q_0}(X, \mathcal{O}(K^\mu))$ and horizontal holomorphic maps $\Phi: S \to X$ arising from variations of Hodge structure: specifically, exhibit a natural pullback / pairing construction that produces, from classes in $H^{q_0}(X,\mathcal{O}(K^\mu))$, holomorphic invariants of such period maps.

(b) Determine whether $H^{q_0}(X,\mathcal{O}(K^\mu))$ can be used to construct sufficiently many automorphic forms on $D$ (i.e., $\Gamma$-invariant holomorphic sections of suitable line bundles over images of period maps) to algebrize the images of period maps, in the sense of realizing closures of period images as quasi-projective algebraic varieties.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made on this circle of questions through work of Griffiths, Green, Kerr, Carayol and others (e.g., "Hodge Domains and Automorphic Cohomology", "Special Values of Automorphic Cohomology Classes", and Kerr's work on cup products in automorphic cohomology for Sp(4)). These works develop Penrose-type transforms relating $H^{q_0}(\Gamma\backslash D,\mathcal{O}(K^\mu))$ to holomorphic data on cycle spaces and to horizontal period maps, and treat low-rank cases (e.g., $SU(2,1)$, $Sp_4$). However, a complete general theory using automorphic cohomology to algebrize images of non-classical period maps remains open.
